svg.text: Five Questions That Set Laura’s Plan

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: January 2027

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: What must never depend on markets?

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: The ten $50,000 payments. $300,000 buys the original ladder, one Treasury for each January, $2,388 short.

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif
'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: January 2028

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: Does the ladder hold if early cash earns nothing?

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: Not alone. The first $39,162 of the second deposit completes it and adds Treasuries.

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: $57,070 gap closed

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: January 2028

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: What can co-sponsors count on?

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: A floor bought now, not later: $81,244 in IBTM, paid out December 2032. $29,594 goes to VT.

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: $95,000 floor

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: January 2031

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: When does Laura name a figure?

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: Only once it is held. Half of VT moves into IBTM, whatever the market has done.

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif
'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif
'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: What is left for Laura?

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: The other half of VT, promised to no one, after a $115,000 contribution.

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: About $28,700

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: From January 2033 the Treasuries are a $445,655 operating reserve that pays each January to 2042.

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: Only a missed deposit or a Treasury default changes the plan. A fall in share prices changes none of these steps.

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: Note. Treasury curve of 6 November 2026. Cash waiting for a payment is assumed to earn nothing, fund payouts are cut by 0.5%

text.font-family: 'Times New Roman', Tinos, 'Liberation Serif', Times, serif

svg.text: and the range is rounded down to $5,000. The ceiling and the amount kept are the central case. Source: Team calculations.
